title: Phetchaburi & Cha-am with Kids 2026 — 3-Day Family Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Phetchaburi & Cha-am family itinerary in Thailand: ride the funicular up Khao Wang, feed sheep at Swiss Sheep Farm, ride a camel, and splash at Cha-am Beach — with times, prices, and tips for travelling with kids.
keywords: Phetchaburi with kids, Cha-am family trip, Khao Wang funicular, Swiss Sheep Farm Cha-am, kid-friendly Phetchaburi attractions
h1:
Phetchaburi & Cha-am with the Family
A 3-Day Plan That Won't Wear Kids Out
intro: Phetchaburi and Cha-am make a great pairing for a trip with kids. They sit just over two hours from Bangkok, and there's plenty here that children actually enjoy — riding the funicular up Khao Wang, feeding sheep, riding a camel, and swimming at Cha-am Beach where the waves stay gentle. This plan alternates walking stretches with sit-down breaks, leaves room for an afternoon nap, and saves a kid-friendly highlight for each day, so the whole family can make the most of the trip without the evening meltdowns.

blocks.html: The tricky part of doing Phetchaburi with kids is that the town has hilltop historic sites you have to climb to, plus a cave with stairs going down — and little ones usually run out of energy before the adults do. The trick is to take the funicular up Khao Wang instead of walking, plan outdoor activities for the morning and late afternoon, and treat the Cha-am side as your beach-and-rest day. This 3-day, 2-night plan splits the trip into two zones — Phetchaburi town and Cha-am — to cut down on driving back and forth. If you're only coming for 2 days and 1 night, you can drop Day 3 entirely.

items: Day 1 (Phetchaburi town) — morning funicular up Khao Wang to see the palace and town views, an afternoon stop at Khao Luang Cave for the light beams, and Phetchaburi's famous sweets in the evening.

Day 2 (Cha-am — animal parks) — feed the sheep at Swiss Sheep Farm in the morning, ride a camel at Camel Republic, swim at Cha-am Beach in the afternoon, and walk the seafront for seafood in the evening.
Day 3 (photos, then home) — morning at Santorini Park for the Ferris wheel and Greek-style photo spots, then pack up and head back in the afternoon.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Funicular up Khao Wang + Khao Luang Cave

items.activity: Arrive in Phetchaburi, check in and drop your bags
items.note: It's about a 2–2.5 hour drive from Bangkok. If you come by train or van into town, you can grab a local ride from there. Dropping your luggage before heading out makes the day much easier.

items.activity: Ride the funicular up Phra Nakhon Khiri (Khao Wang)
items.note: The electric funicular runs both ways — about 80 THB for adults, 15 THB for kids — open 08:30–16:30. Kids love this part because they get to ride up the hill instead of climbing a long flight of stairs. At the top there's a royal hall and views over Phetchaburi town. Watch out for monkeys snatching things while you walk around — keep food and water bottles tucked away.

items.activity: Come back down, lunch somewhere indoors
items.note: Pick an air-conditioned spot near the base of the hill to give the kids a break from the sun. Phetchaburi town has plenty of inexpensive rice-and-curry shops and noodle places.

Entry is around 40 THB, open roughly 09:00–16:00. Inside, openings in the ceiling let beams of sunlight stream down beautifully (best mid-morning, around 09:30–10:30, but you can still see them in the afternoon). The way down into the cave is a stone staircase, so hold the kids' hands. There are lots of monkeys around — mind your belongings.

Phetchaburi is known for sweets made from toddy-palm sugar, like khanom mo kaeng (baked custard), thong yip and thong yot. Kids tend to love them, and they make easy gifts to take home. A relaxed way to close out the first day before heading back to the hotel.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Feed Sheep, Ride a Camel + Swim at Cha-am Beach

items.note: Entry is about 50 THB for adults, around 30 THB for kids over 80 cm tall, open 09:00–17:00. There are sheep to feed, European-style photo spots, and wide lawns for kids to run around. Little ones especially love the sheep-feeding part.

Entry is about 120 THB for Thai adults; kids under 100 cm get in free. It's done up in a Moroccan style, with camel rides, pony rides, giraffe feeding and rides. Older kids will enjoy the wider range of activities. It's right next to the sheep farm, so you can do both back to back.

items.activity: Lunch, then back to the hotel for the kids' nap
items.note: The afternoon sun is at its harshest now. Resting in an air-conditioned room to save energy for the evening beach beats pushing through the midday heat.

Cha-am's waves are gentle and the water is shallow, which makes it good for kids. You can rent rubber rings, and there are banana boats and beach pony rides for older children. The seafront road is lined with shady pines and is nice for a cycle. Coming in the late afternoon, the softer sun is kinder to kids' skin.
Seafood restaurants line the whole seafront road. Pick one with sea-view tables so the kids can watch the waves while they eat — an easy, relaxed dinner to end the day.

Entry is around 150 THB and includes one ride. It's styled after Santorini in blue and white, with a Ferris wheel about 40 metres tall for the views. Kids love the rides and the photogenic corners. Come early while it's still quiet and the sun is mild.

items.activity: Lunch at a mall or air-conditioned restaurant
items.note: Pick an air-conditioned spot to let the kids rest before the long drive. Keep this meal relaxed — no need to rush.

items.activity: Stop for Phetchaburi sweets, then drive back
items.note: Khanom mo kaeng and toddy-palm sugar are easy gifts to grab on the way home. Leaving before mid-afternoon helps you avoid the evening traffic — and the kids usually fall asleep in the car right about then.

blocks.title: Tips for Doing Phetchaburi & Cha-am with Kids
blocks.html: Take the funicular up Khao Wang instead of walking — it saves the kids a lot of energy · Bring hats, drinking water and sunscreen, since many spots are out in the open with no shade · Build in an afternoon nap for little ones every day to avoid evening meltdowns · Watch for monkeys at Khao Wang and Khao Luang Cave — keep food tucked away and don't let kids walk around holding snacks in the open.

blocks.text: What Kind of Stay Works for Families

blocks.html: For families with kids, staying on the Cha-am–Hua Hin side works best, since there are beachfront resorts and hotels with pools the kids can splash in come evening. Pick somewhere near the beach so you can walk down to the water easily. For the first day in Phetchaburi town, it's about a 40-minute drive from Cha-am — so if you'd rather not change hotels, you can base yourself in Cha-am and just drive in and back.

items.name: Beachfront Resort in Cha-am
items.blurb: Walk straight down to the water, with a pool and family rooms — a good place for kids to unwind after a full day out, right by the sea.

items.name: Hotel in Phetchaburi Town
items.blurb: Close to Khao Wang and Khao Luang Cave, saving travel time on the first day. A good pick if you want a full day in town before moving on to Cha-am.

faq.q: How many days is right for Phetchaburi & Cha-am with young kids?
faq.a: Two days and one night is about right for young kids — enough to fit in the funicular up Khao Wang, feeding the sheep, and swimming at Cha-am Beach without overdoing it. If you want to add photos at Santorini Park and keep the pace easy, stretch it to 3 days and 2 nights.

faq.q: Do you have to climb stairs up Khao Wang with kids, and how much is the funicular?
faq.a: You don't have to walk up — there's an electric funicular for the ride up and down, about 80 THB for adults and 15 THB for kids, open 08:30–16:30. Most kids love the ride up the hill. At the top you can walk around the palace and take in the town views, but hold the kids' hands and watch for the monkeys nearby.

faq.q: How much is entry to Swiss Sheep Farm and Camel Republic in Cha-am, and what can kids do there?
faq.a: Swiss Sheep Farm is about 50 THB for adults and around 30 THB for kids over 80 cm; there are sheep to feed and lawns to run around on. Camel Republic is about 120 THB for Thai adults, with kids under 100 cm free; it has camel rides, pony rides, giraffe feeding and rides. The two are right next to each other, so you can do both in a single morning.

faq.q: Is Cha-am Beach good for kids to swim, and what activities are there?
faq.a: Yes — Cha-am's waves are gentle and the water is shallow, so kids can swim safely with an adult watching nearby. You can rent rubber rings, there are beach pony rides and banana boats for older kids, and the seafront road has a line of pines that's nice for cycling. Going in the late afternoon, when the sun is softer, is kinder to kids' skin.

faq.q: What times should families avoid in Phetchaburi & Cha-am?
faq.a: Avoid sightseeing in the midday sun, roughly 12:00–15:00, since open spots like the farms and the beach get very hot and kids tire quickly. Get out in the morning and late afternoon, and leave time for a rest or nap in an air-conditioned room in the early afternoon — it lets the whole family keep going longer.
